findings.description: Endpoint 'GET /accounts/{accountId}' accesses resources by ID but lacks explicit user-scoped authorization checks. Attackers may manipulate object IDs to access unauthorized data.
findings.evidence: Path parameter(s) found without user-scoping: ['accountId']
findings.impact: Unauthorized access to other users' data, leading to data breaches and privacy violations.
findings.remediation: Implement object-level authorization checks for every request. Use indirect object references and verify the authenticated user owns or is authorized to access the requested resource.
findings.detection_reason: Path parameter with 'id' pattern detected without user-scoping authorization context in the endpoint security definition.
findings.false_positive_note: This is a potential vulnerability identified through static analysis of the API specification. Manual verification is recommended to confirm exploitability in the deployed environment.

findings.description: Endpoint 'POST /auth/login' does not require authentication. This allows anonymous access to potentially sensitive operations.
findings.evidence: No security requirements defined. Auth type: None
findings.impact: Attackers can perform unauthorized actions, access sensitive data, and potentially take over accounts.
findings.remediation: Enforce authentication on all endpoints that require user identification. Use industry-standard authentication mechanisms (OAuth 2.0, JWT). Implement proper token validation and expiration.
findings.detection_reason: Endpoint accepts state-changing HTTP methods (POST) without any security requirements defined in the OpenAPI specification.
findings.false_positive_note: This is a potential vulnerability identified through static analysis of the API specification. Manual verification is recommended to confirm exploitability in the deployed environment.

findings.description: GET endpoint '/accounts/{accountId}' does not define pagination parameters. Without limits, clients can request unbounded datasets.
findings.evidence: No limit/page/offset parameters found in endpoint definition.
findings.impact: Denial of service through resource exhaustion. Large data retrieval can overwhelm databases and network bandwidth.
findings.remediation: Implement mandatory pagination with configurable page sizes. Add rate limiting per user/IP. Enforce maximum result set limits.
findings.detection_reason: GET endpoint does not define pagination parameters (limit, page, offset), indicating potential for unbounded data retrieval.
findings.false_positive_note: This is a potential vulnerability identified through static analysis of the API specification. Manual verification is recommended to confirm exploitability in the deployed environment.

findings.description: Authentication-related endpoint 'POST /auth/login' does not define rate limiting (HTTP 429) controls.
findings.evidence: No 429 Too Many Requests response defined on POST /auth/login
findings.impact: Brute-force attacks on credentials, OTP guessing, and account enumeration are unmitigated.
findings.remediation: Enforce per-IP/per-account rate limiting with account lockout, CAPTCHA, and monitor for credential stuffing.
findings.detection_reason: Endpoint '/auth/login' is authentication-related and lacks a 429 rate-limit response definition.
findings.false_positive_note: This is a potential vulnerability identified through static analysis of the API specification. Manual verification is recommended to confirm exploitability in the deployed environment.

findings.description: Endpoint 'POST /webhooks' accepts URL-type parameters (['url']) that could be exploited for Server-Side Request Forgery.

findings.impact: Attackers can make the server send requests to internal services, access cloud metadata endpoints, or exfiltrate data from internal networks.
findings.remediation: Validate and sanitize all URL inputs against an allowlist. Use a dedicated URL validation library. Restrict outbound network access. Block internal IP ranges and metadata endpoints.
findings.detection_reason: Parameter(s) ['url'] accept URL-type input that could be used to make server-side requests to arbitrary destinations.
findings.false_positive_note: This is a potential vulnerability identified through static analysis of the API specification. Manual verification is recommended to confirm exploitability in the deployed environment.
